records.title: Establishment of a Multi-Stage In Vitro Screening Platform to Identify Candidate Compounds for Intestinal Mucosal Damage in Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
records.abstract: Mucosal healing is a key therapeutic goal in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), which is characterized by mucosal lesions in the gastrointestinal tract. For IBD drug development, it is important to identify multiple compounds with strong effects on mucosal injury and different mechanisms of action. Here, we established an intestinal organoid-based assay to evaluate cytokine-induced inflammatory and epithelial stress responses. We also developed an intestinal microphysiological system (intestinal MPS)-based assay for quantitative evaluation of cytokine-induced changes in mucosal architecture. By integrating these assays, we constructed a multi-stage screening platform to identify candidate compounds that suppress inflammatory responses and preserve mucosal architecture. Tofacitinib, an approved IBD drug, showed positive effects in these assays, supporting the relevance of this platform. Although organoid-based screening identified pimitespib as a candidate compound, pimitespib did not improve mucosal architecture in the intestinal MPS. Consistently, pimitespib failed to restore mucosal morphology in an IBD mouse model. These findings suggest that combining intestinal organoids with an intestinal MPS may help identify candidate compounds that suppress inflammatory responses while preserving mucosal architecture.

records.title: A synNotch-based morphogen detection system reveals sFRP2 enhances Wnt3a signaling.
records.abstract: Morphogen gradients provide essential positional information during tissue development, yet the extracellular mechanisms that regulate morphogen transport remain elusive. Here, we introduce a mechanosensitive detection system based on synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptors that selectively detect surface-bound morphogens. Applying this platform to Wnt signaling, we demonstrate that secreted Frizzled-related protein 2 (sFRP2) promotes the recruitment of Wnt3a to the cell surface via heparan sulfate proteoglycans, enabling robust activation of canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Notably, sFRP2 extends the effective signaling range of Wnt3a under ligand-limiting conditions. In intestinal organoid cultures, sFRP2 enhances Wnt3a-driven growth and induces high-Wnt morphological states even at low Wnt3a concentrations. These findings identify sFRP2 as an extracellular carrier that stabilizes surface-bound Wnt3a and regulates both the strength and spatial range of Wnt signaling. Broadly, this work demonstrates the utility of synNotch mechano-sensing for dissecting extracellular morphogen dynamics and highlights the potential of morphogen carrier proteins to optimize organoid culture.

records.title: VEGF-A-Dependent Vascular Signaling Modulates BMSC-Derived Cartilaginous Organoid Fate During Endochondral Spinal Bone Regeneration.
records.abstract: Spinal bone regeneration is hindered by early avascularity and incomplete integration with host bone. We investigated whether BMSC-derived cartilaginous organoids could serve as developmental templates whose cartilage-to-bone transition is modulated by VEGF-A-associated vascular signaling. Mouse BMSCs were assembled into cartilaginous organoids and evaluated through in vitro vascular modulation, ectopic implantation, and a mouse spinal bone defect model. VEGF-A signaling was manipulated using HUVEC coculture, recombinant VEGF-A165, or VEGF-A neutralization. The organoids progressively matured into hypertrophy-competent cartilaginous tissues with enhanced matrix deposition and hypertrophic characteristics. HUVEC coculture and VEGF-A stimulation enhanced vascular-associated maturation and promoted the cartilage-to-bone transition, whereas VEGF-A neutralization attenuated these effects. In vivo, VEGF-A promoted vascularization, hypertrophic remodeling, ectopic mineralization, and bone formation, whereas anti-VEGF preserved cartilage and reduced ossification. In spinal defects, organoid-loaded GelMA enhanced bone regeneration and host-repair integration, with VEGF-A further improving structural repair, whereas anti-VEGF reduced regenerative outcomes. These findings suggest that VEGF-A-associated vascular signaling modulates cartilaginous organoid fate and supports developmental organoid grafting as a potential strategy for spinal bone regeneration. Further studies are warranted to clarify the relative contributions of endothelial-associated and direct VEGF-A responses, thereby refining the mechanistic understanding of vascular regulation during cartilaginous organoid maturation and endochondral bone regeneration.

records.title: Generation of depolarization-responsive dental stem cell-derived neural-like spheroids using a micropatterned chip platform.
records.abstract: Dental stem cells represent an accessible adult stem cell source with neuronal affinity due to their cranial neural crest origin, yet dental-derived neural-like spheroid models often suffer from heterogeneous differentiation, limited organization, and poor reproducibility. Here, we established a stepwise workflow to induce neurogenic differentiation of dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and organize them into spatially controlled, depolarization-responsive neural-like spheroids using a micropatterned culture platform. Seven-day neurogenic induction generated Neuro-DPSCs with marked morphological remodeling, neurite-like processes, and increased expression of neural lineage markers including TUJ1, NSE, MAP2, NeuN, and NEFM. In 3D culture, Neuro-DPSCs self-assembled into spheroidal aggregates, while substrate wettability strongly influenced aggregation and outgrowth. Hydrophobic surfaces promoted spheroid formation but limited long-term maintenance due to free-floating aggregation. To improve spatial control, a micropatterned platform was applied to define adhesive contact points, constrain spheroid positioning, and guide inter-spheroid neurite-like network formation. The resulting spheroids showed enrichment of gene networks associated with neurite-like organization, axon guidance, synaptic vesicle biology, neurotransmitter-related pathways, and receptor signaling, together with KCl-induced depolarization-responsive calcium activity. These findings demonstrate that neurogenic priming combined with micropattern-guided assembly provides a controllable workflow for generating spatially organized neural-like DPSC spheroids.

records.title: Clinical and research perspectives on pharmacogenetics and theratyping in pulmonology: A narrative review.
records.abstract: Chronic respiratory diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), cystic fibrosis (CF), pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD)-related emphysema, show substantial interindividual variability in treatment response. Pharmacogenetics and theratyping provide a framework for improving therapeutic stratification, although their clinical applicability across respiratory diseases remains uneven. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from international guidelines and literature published between 2000 and 2025 on pharmacogenetic determinants of drug response and functional theratyping approaches in major chronic pulmonary diseases, with emphasis on clinical validity, implementation readiness, and translational relevance. Among respiratory conditions, only CFTR genotyping in CF and SERPINA1 testing in AATD-related emphysema currently meet criteria for routine clinical implementation. In asthma, COPD, and PAH, multiple candidate pharmacogenetic associations, including ADRB2, CRHR1, CYP3A5, CYP2C9, IL4R, IL5RA, and BMPR2-related pathways, remain investigational and require prospective validation. Functional theratyping using patient-derived epithelial cells or organoids expands treatment eligibility in rare CFTR variants and illustrates a model for future precision approaches in chronic lung disease. Environmental and modifiable factors, including tobacco smoke exposure, adherence, infection control, and air pollution, may further influence treatment response and should be considered when interpreting pharmacogenetic associations. Pharmacogenetics is already transforming clinical management in selected monogenic respiratory conditions and is likely to expand into complex chronic pulmonary diseases as evidence matures. Wider implementation will depend on prospective validation studies, integration into clinical decision-support systems, equitable access to testing, and improved clinician training in genomic medicine.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: scREFINE: Label-efficient refinement of frozen scGPT embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) clustering remains challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, technical noise, and limited cell annotations. Here, we propose scREFINE, a label-efficient semi-supervised clustering framework that adapts pretrained single-cell foundation-model embeddings for accurate cell clustering. scREFINE uses a lightweight refinement head to map cells into a task-specific clustering space using only 5% labeled cells, while treating the remaining cells as unlabeled during training. To exploit information from unlabeled cells, scREFINE introduces stability-aware soft structural regularization over local neighborhoods, which leverages reliable cell-cell relations as auxiliary guidance without relying on hard pseudo-label constraints. Experiments on five benchmark scRNA-seq datasets show that scREFINE achieves the best ARI on every dataset against every baseline under an identical, leakage-free protocol (mean ± SD over four seeds). A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the five per-dataset means yields p=0.0625, above the conventional 0.05 threshold because only five datasets are available; we therefore interpret the consistent improvements as strong empirical evidence rather than a statistically conclusive demonstration. A common-embedding comparison confirms that these gains arise from task-specific refinement rather than the pretrained representation alone: adapted baselines receiving identical embeddings achieve 0.00-0.61 ARI, compared with 0.73-0.89 for scREFINE. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that task-specific embedding refinement is the primary driver of improvement, whereas soft structural regularization provides dataset-dependent auxiliary gains and degrades more gracefully than hard pseudo-labels when supervision is scarce. Biological marker-gene analysis confirms that the predicted clusters correspond to canonical cell populations.

records.title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network.
records.abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts.
records.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

records.title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models.
records.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

records.title: Chemical Biology in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: From Ligand Discovery to Virtual Cells.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how scientists, including chemical biologists, conduct research. This review is intended to serve as an introduction for chemical biologists to applications of artificial intelligence in chemical biology. We review how chemical and biological data are featurized, the types of models commonly used in chemical biology applications, challenges in assessing accuracy of artificial intelligence models, and recent developments in agentic artificial intelligence for autonomous research. The applications we will cover include protein structure prediction, ligand discovery, peptide and protein design, prediction of mutational effects, interactomics and gene regulation, and virtual cells.

records.title: An AI-designed, recombinantly produced FtsZ-directed peptide with in vitro activity against pan-drug-resistant clinical isolates.
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is outpacing the antibiotic pipeline, yet antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) - the most-cited alternative class - remain constrained by proteolytic instability, host toxicity, and the cost of solid-phase synthesis. We report an integrated design-to-validation pipeline that addresses these constraints and yields a de novo peptide directed at an intracellular, non-lytic target. Instead of relying on membrane disruption, the design was directed at FtsZ, the essential bacterial cell-division GTPase, at a consensus epitope (residues 60-145) that our alignments show is substantially more conserved across the Gram-positive/Gram-negative divide than FtsZ overall (68.6% versus 50.1% identity between Enterococcus and Klebsiella orthologues) while sharing only approximately 8-24% identity with human tubulin. A sequence-space diffusion model conditioned on the amino-acid composition of experimentally validated AMPs generated ten binders; fusion to 120 cell-penetrating motifs, machine-learning triage, co-folding and replicated molecular dynamics identified a single lead, Combined111. Rather than chemical synthesis, the peptide was produced biologically: the codon-optimised gene was cloned in-house into pHT254 and expressed as an intracellular, C-terminal 8xHis-tagged product in the protease-deficient Bacillus subtilis WB800N host, giving a mean transcript induction of 3.40-fold (SD 2.01, n = 4 biological replicates) and a single band of approximately 11.1 kDa after one-step Ni-NTA purification. Against one pan-drug-resistant clinical isolate of each of seven species, the purified peptide produced larger inhibition zones than a panel of last-resort antibiotics for five of the seven, by a mean of 4.81 mm, although this difference was not statistically significant (95% CI -0.64 to 10.27; t(6) = 2.16, p = 0.074, Cohen's dz = 0.82). Each zone value is a single measurement, so reproducibility was not assessed, and inhibition-zone diameters are not a direct measure of comparative potency. The advantage was consistent in direction but not uniform, the pan-drug-resistant Enterococcus faecalis isolate being the least susceptible. E. faecium FtsZ was the sequence used for the computational design, whereas the Gram-positive organism available for experimental testing was E. faecalis. These findings show that generative design can be coupled to low-cost bacterial expression in one laboratory. FtsZ-directed inhibition is presented here as a hypothesis rather than an established mechanism: target engagement was inferred from alignment, co-folding and molecular dynamics, and no direct binding measurement, FtsZ polymerisation or GTPase assay, or Z-ring localisation experiment was performed. Minimum inhibitory concentrations, resistance selection, haemolysis, mammalian cytotoxicity, and in vivo efficacy all remain to be established.

records.title: PRIZM: combining low-N data and zero-shot models to design enhanced protein variants.
records.abstract: Machine learning has repeatedly shown the ability to accelerate protein engineering, but many approaches demand large amounts of robust, high-quality training data as well as substantial computational expertise. While large pre-trained models can function as zero-shot proxies for predicting variant effects, selecting the best model for a given protein property is often non-trivial. Here, we introduce Protein Ranking using Informed Zero-shot Modelling (PRIZM), a two-phase workflow that first uses a high-quality low-N dataset to identify the most suitable pre-trained zero-shot model for a target protein property and then applies that model to rank and prioritize an in silico variant library for experimental testing. Across diverse benchmark datasets spanning multiple protein properties, PRIZM reliably separated low- from high-performing models using datasets of ∼20 labelled variants. We further demonstrate PRIZM in enzyme engineering case studies targeting sucrose synthase thermostability and glycosyltransferase activity, where PRIZM-guided selection identified improved variants, including gains of ∼3°C in apparent melting temperature and ∼20% higher relative activity. PRIZM provides an accessible, data-efficient route to leverage foundation models for protein design while requiring minimal experimental data. PRIZM is publicly available via Zenodo, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23035983, and the PRIZM GitHub repository https://github.com/daha-la/PRIZM.

records.title: Tuned Fitness Landscapes for Benchmarking Model-Guided Protein Design.
records.abstract: Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of synthetic landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP ("Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins") for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at https://github.com/google-research/slip.

records.title: AI-Assisted Molecular Structure Prediction from Tandem Mass Spectra: Reliability and Validation.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has broadened the interpretation of tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) beyond experimental library matching, enabling molecular fingerprint prediction, candidate ranking, and generation of previously unlisted structures. Yet these outputs do not all support the same claim about chemical identity. This review briefly summarizes database-restricted retrieval, database-free generation, and scaffold-guided hybrid methods, and then asks what additional evidence is needed to turn a plausible structure into a defensible annotation. We examine failure modes involving incomplete candidate spaces, erroneous precursor assignments, structurally related isomers, leakage between training and test data, and misinterpreted confidence scores. The review contributes two practical elements: a candidate-discrimination workflow, in which alternative structures are retained and targeted measurements such as multienergy fragmentation, retention behavior, ion mobility, and authentic standards are selected according to the unresolved structural question; and an evidence-to-claim checklist that links each question to the most informative measurement and to the strongest supportable identification confidence level. Both synthesize established analytical principles for small-molecule electrospray LC-HRMS/MS rather than constituting a validated scoring algorithm. By making the basis of each annotation transparent, they are intended to improve the practical value of AI-assisted MS/MS in metabolomics, pharmaceutical analysis, environmental screening, and forensic toxicology.

records.title: Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia.
records.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a premier model for precision medicine, having moved from genetic discovery to approved therapeutics within two decades. Yet despite the clinical success of monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNA and the newly approved oral macrocyclic-peptide inhibitor class, targeting PCSK9 remains a demanding biophysical challenge. Clinical translation has concentrated almost entirely on the rigid, well-resolved subtilisin-like catalytic domain that interfaces with the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). By contrast, the C-terminal cysteine- and histidine-rich domain (CHRD), which governs allosteric regulation, protein trafficking and post-translational modification, is highly disordered and largely elusive in experimental structures, leaving a critical regulatory network therapeutically unexploited. This review examines how advanced computational biology is bridging that structural gap, organizing the computational landscape of PCSK9 around the biophysical mechanisms of gain- and loss-of-function variants. We detail how explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations and cryptic-pocket detection expose the functional plasticity and allosteric networks that static crystallography cannot capture, and we evaluate the convergence of these physics-based approaches with artificial intelligence, including deep-learning structure prediction and generative design of de novo nanobody and peptide binders. Therapeutic development and the structural literature currently point in diverging directions: drug discovery remains focused on the crowded LDLR-binding interface, whereas computational methods are beginning to identify candidate sites beyond it. We argue that the next advance in PCSK9 therapeutics will come from integrating generative artificial intelligence with rigorous enhanced sampling in a unified pipeline, deliberately shifting focus toward the disordered regulatory domains that have evaded classical screening.

records.title: Fluctuating Methylation-based ctDNA Detection in NSCLC Surveillance: Implications for Serial Monitoring and Specificity.
records.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) addresses key limitations of traditional radiographic and tissue-based screening by providing a noninvasive alternative for the surveillance of NSCLC. In our study, we aim to evaluate trends in the performance of a commercially available methylation-based ctDNA test, characterize patient factors associated with fluctuating ctDNA positivity, and evaluate the clinical implications of serial monitoring. This retrospective observational cohort study included patients who underwent lung resection or stereotactic body radiation therapy for NSCLC followed by posttreatment ctDNA testing from 2024 to 2025. The primary outcomes include patient- and tumor-related risk factors associated with ctDNA positivity. A subgroup analysis of the ctDNA-positive group evaluated clinical events and genomic profiling that may influence transient ctDNA positivity. Of the 85 patients studied, 17 (20%) had at least one positive ctDNA test. Both ctDNA-positive and negative groups had similar patient and tumor-related features. Ten (59%) patients with a positive result subsequently tested negative, and 11 (65%) had a ctDNA tumor fraction near the limit of detection (LOD) without radiographic recurrence. No consistent associations were found with timing, adjuvant therapy, inflammatory markers, or tumor genomics. Three patients with ctDNA fractions above the limit of detection had confirmed recurrence; none in the ctDNA-negative group had disease recurrence. Although the utility of serial ctDNA testing is promising for NSCLC surveillance, isolated low-level positivity may not warrant clinical action. We observe frequent low-level, transient ctDNA positivity without radiographic evidence of recurrence, suggesting limitations in assay specificity and need for trend-based interpretation instead of isolated testing.

records.title: Is liquid biopsy in oncology cost-effective? A comparative analysis and systematic review.
records.abstract: To describe cost-effectiveness trends in oncological liquid biopsy (LB) through harmonized comparative analyses across countries, cancer types, technologies, and clinical applications. Economic evaluations reporting incremental costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) for oncological LB-related strategies and comparators. MEDLINE (via PubMed) and Cochrane Library. Study quality was assessed using CHEQUE, with mean methodological and reporting scores of 79.7% and 85.5%, respectively. Economic inputs were harmonized to EUR 2024. Incremental net monetary benefit (INMB) was recalculated under eight willingness-to-pay (WTP) criteria, using median INMB as the primary descriptive outcome. Complementary analyses examined the so-called ΔWTP% (i.e., the percentage ratio between the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) and the WTP threshold), means, subgroups, scenario eligibility, and sensitivity to WTP selection. Twenty-one studies contributed 43 modeled scenarios. Median INMB was positive under all eight WTP criteria (+€79.52 to +€5091.21 per patient); eight scenarios were dominant. Seventeen scenarios (39.53%) changed economic classification across thresholds. INMB and ΔWTP% agreed in all 328 eligible scenario-threshold comparisons. Under the common Italian GDP×2 WTP, 79.07% of scenarios and 96.97% of subgroups had favorable INMB, with an overall median of +€1560.07 per patient. Two cost-saving scenarios with negative QALYs highlighted ethical and distributional trade-offs. Differences in clinical pathways, model assumptions, and local costs, together with non-independent scenarios and unavailable patient-level data, limit setting-specific interpretation. LB showed broadly favorable but context-dependent economic potential. Median INMB and complementary sensitivity analyses support transparent comparisons; clinical implementation requires locally calibrated evaluation. No external funding. records.title: Circulating tumor DNA as a tool for precision management in bladder cancer: A narrative review.
records.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a potential paradigm-shifting biomarker for precision management of bladder cancer, particularly muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). Although ctDNA assays are not yet widely implemented in routine clinical practice, a growing body of evidence supports its utility in diagnosis, risk stratification, prognosis, therapeutic decision-making and post-treatment surveillance. This review summarizes the current and evolving roles of ctDNA in bladder cancer management, with particular emphasis on completed and ongoing clinical trials that are shaping its integration into standard care. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, Google Scholar, Embase, and Scopus for studies published between January 2005 and November 2025. The search strategy included the following terms: bladder cancer, circulating tumor DNA, liquid biopsy, circulating biomarkers. A total of 172 English-language records were initially identified. After screening for relevance to the objectives of this review, 29 studies met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed in detail. In bladder cancer, ctDNA has demonstrated prognostic value across multiple disease stages, including diagnosis, assessment of response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, and surveillance post-cystectomy. In the adjuvant setting, ctDNA-positivity has been associated with improved outcomes when patients are subsequently treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, as shown in the IMvigor010 trial and further explored in the ongoing IMvigor011 trial. Ongoing studies (e.g. MODERN and TOMBOLA) aim to further validate ctDNA-guided treatment strategies, and their role in prognostication and disease monitoring. Multiple studies and ongoing trials have established the utility of ctDNA in the realm of bladder cancer with indications spanning detection of recurrence, guiding use of adjuvant therapy, and prognosis evaluation. Despite this momentum, several barriers continue to limit broader clinical integration, including high testing costs, absence of standardized assay protocols, and significant inter-laboratory variability. Addressing these challenges through robust clinical trials and standardized regulatory frameworks will be essential for the widespread and reliable adoption of ctDNA in bladder cancer care.

records.title: Circulating tRNA-derived small RNAs as cancer biomarkers: appraising the evidence by intended use and validation level.
records.abstract: Reliable biomarkers for cancer early detection, prognostic stratification, recurrence surveillance, and treatment-response prediction remain clinically insufficient. tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) are abundant, structurally compact, and recurrently dysregulated in malignancy, and have been widely proposed as liquid-biopsy analytes. Their biogenesis, mechanisms, and therapeutic prospects have been reviewed extensively. What has not been assessed is whether the reported clinical evidence supports the claims attached to it, and that is the question this review addresses. We appraise published circulating tsRNA studies against four criteria that govern progression toward clinical use: analytical validity, cohort design and comparator choice, independent validation, and demonstrated incremental clinical utility. Biology is summarized only where it bears on measurement-the distinct enzymatic routes that generate tRNA-derived fragments and tRNA halves, the terminal chemistries they impose, the modifications that bias library construction, and the extracellular biology that determines what is actually quantified in blood. Candidates are then re-classified by intended use and graded by validation level in a structured evidence table reporting cohort size, comparator group, platform, normalization, diagnostic performance, and validation status. Most candidates rest on single-center retrospective case-control comparisons against healthy donors. Detection in stage I disease has been conflated with early detection, and postoperative decline with rcrrence monitoring. Disease specificity is frequently untested, notably for glycine-GCC-derived fragments, which also rise in active inflammatory bowel disease. No circulating tsRNA has yet demonstrated incremental clinical value in a prospectively validated setting. tsRNAs remain a biologically compelling and analytically tractable biomarker reservoir. Realizing that potential will require standardized pre-analytics, clinically relevant comparators, transfer to analytically validated targeted assays, and independent multicenter validation. We provide a minimum reporting checklist and a nomenclature cross-walk to support this.

records.title: Unifying functional experimental systems with clinical predictive technologies for personalized care in PDAC.
records.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a clinical challenge, projected to become the second leading cause of cancer-related death by 2030. Traditional research has historically relied on established PDAC-derived cell lines to establish 2D in vitro models or in vivo xenografts for drug discovery. These approaches, however, fail to encompass the complexity of PDAC and few studies have been translated into game-changing treatments for patients with pancreatic cancer. This review advocates for a paradigm shift through the integration of complementary modeling strategies. We provide a comprehensive evaluation of more sophisticated in vitro systems, such as 3D models (spheroids and organoids), co-cultures and microfluidics, which offer scalable platforms for high-throughput screening and mechanistic analysis. Likewise, we emphasize the indispensable role of in vivo models, including genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs) for studying stepwise progression and immune evasion, and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) for capturing human-specific drug sensitivities and intratumoral heterogeneity. Beyond functional models, we explore the clinical utility of transcriptomic profiling to define PDAC subtypes, facilitating real-time patient stratification in landmark clinical trials. We further examine the role of liquid biopsy as a dynamic tool for monitoring minimal residual disease and the emergence of treatment resistance. Finally, we discuss the future of pharmacogenomics, the "tri-genomic" influence of the microbiome, and the integration of multi-omics through artificial intelligence to optimize individual therapeutic outcomes. By unifying these diverse predictive paradigms, we aim to bridge the gap between preclinical discovery and precision oncology, fostering more effective and individualized treatment strategies for all PDAC patients.

records.title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation.
records.abstract: A fundamental challenge in human genetics is determining how regulatory genetic variation shapes complex traits and disease risk. Chromatin quantitative trait loci can link disease-associated variants to regulatory element activity, but mapping them in disease-relevant tissues at scale remains challenging. We leverage epigenomic liquid biopsy by profiling histone modifications in circulating chromatin from 328 cancer patients and 38 healthy individuals to identify cell-free chromatin quantitative trait loci. These loci affect regulatory element activities from diverse non-hematologic tissues and developmentally restricted elements reactivated in cancer. Through cistrome-wide association studies, we link 4891 loci to 1011 traits and diseases. Developmentally restricted loci absent in white blood cells are associated with 22.7 traits per 100 quantitative trait loci, compared to 0.58 for white-blood-cell-restricted chromatin quantitative trait loci. Here, we show that cell-free chromatin enables efficient and scalable discovery of regulatory genetic effects across tissues, diseases, and populations.
